key_insight: Weekly blood microsampling and transcriptomic profiling detected interferon-related signals that rose before and during dermatomyositis flares.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help flag impending flare sooner than routine clinical follow-up, supporting more proactive monitoring in dermatomyositis.
method: 6 women with inactive/minimally active dermatomyositis were followed for 6 months
Patients self-reported disease activity weekly; flares were defined by PtGA increase >2 for 2 consecutive weeks
Weekly 125 uL blood microsamples were collected and analyzed by RNA sequencing at 9 timepoints
evidence_signal: Among 54 RNA-seq samples, flare-associated samples showed significantly higher interferon scores, and pathway analysis found enrichment of interferon-related gene sets in pre-flare and flare periods.
watch_item: Very small feasibility study (6 patients, 3 flares) and limited follow-up mean the findings need validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Longitudinal interferon signatures are associated with disease flare in dermatomyositis
